standard_prerequisites.name: Local structure of a morphism locally of finite type over an affine base
standard_prerequisites.reference: More on Morphisms, Stacks tags 057K and 057L, invoked at proof lines 536-539

core_obligations: Reduce to X and S affine by replacing f : X -> S with f|_U : U -> V for affine open neighbourhoods U of x and V of s and F by F|_U (proof lines 527-532).

Settle the case X_s = Supp(F_s) by taking the commutative diagram supplied by the local structure of the finite type morphism and setting Z' = X', i = id, G = g*F, so that affineness, finite presentation of i, i_*G = g*F, finiteness of pi with pi^{-1}({y'}) = {z'}, pure transcendence of kappa(y')/kappa(s') and smoothness of h of relative dimension n with geometrically integral fibres all hold (proof lines 534-549).

In general, first cut Z_s = Supp(F_s) out of X by a closed immersion Z -> X of finite presentation with a finite type module G on Z such that i_*G = F; apply the previous case to Z -> S and G; then embed Z' into a scheme etale over X x_S S' by applying the etale lifting lemma to the composite Z' -> Z x_S S' -> X x_S S' with X' affine, and verify that the completed diagram is a solution of the original problem (proof lines 551-594).
proof_roadmap: Affine reduction: shrink S to an affine neighbourhood V of s and X to an affine neighbourhood U of x inside f^{-1}(V); it suffices to treat f|_U : U -> V with F|_U (proof lines 527-532).

Case X_s = Supp(F_s): the local structure of the finite type morphism yields affine X', Y', S' with an elementary etale neighbourhood of source and base and h : Y' -> S' smooth of relative dimension n with geometrically integral fibres; the trivial closed immersion Z' = X' with G = g*F completes the required diagram (proof lines 534-549).

General case, first stage: produce i : Z -> X a closed immersion of finite presentation and G a finite type module on Z with i_*G = F and Z_s = Supp(F_s), then apply the previous case to Z -> S and G, obtaining Z', Y', S' and z' (proof lines 551-564).

General case, second stage: the composite Z' -> Z x_S S' -> X x_S S' is etale followed by a closed immersion of affines, so the etale lifting lemma gives an etale X' -> X x_S S' of affines with Z' = Z x_X X'; taking x' over z' and completing the diagram with i and pi yields a solution (proof lines 566-594).
difficulty_reason: The lemma demands a whole commutative diagram of pointed schemes at once: affine elementary etale neighbourhoods (S', s') -> (S, s) and (X', x') -> (X, x), a closed immersion i : Z' -> X' of finite presentation with i_*G = g*F, a finite pi : Z' -> Y' with pi^{-1}({y'}) = {z'}, pure transcendence of kappa(y')/kappa(s'), and h : Y' -> S' smooth of relative dimension n = dim_x Supp(F_s) with geometrically integral fibres (statement lines 500-524). The proof splits on whether X_s equals Supp(F_s); the second case is the part that cannot be done routinely, because the closed subscheme Z' coming from the support of F_s must be embedded into a scheme etale over X x_S S' by applying the etale lifting lemma to Z' -> Z x_S S' -> X x_S S' while keeping X' affine (proof lines 566-584). The chapter's own lead-in at lines 441-443 advertises this very lemma as the key technical lemma that makes many later arguments of the chapter work, and later lemmas of the chapter (one step devissage, complete devissage) consume it as their engine.
